name: The Red Feast
about: A great lord invites a rival house to a wedding feast to end their feud, and you are invited too. A servant whispers that the music is a signal. Go, warn them, or stay away and let it happen.
title: The Red Feast at {hall}

beats.speaker: host
beats.text: {host} invites {guest} and all of {guest.house} to a wedding at {hall} to end the feud between them. The King is invited too.

court.text: {guest} of {guest.house}: "{host} offers peace and a wedding, Your Grace. I mean to accept. Will the crown honour the feast with its presence?"

options.label: The King will attend the wedding
options.result: The King accepts. {host} sends word that the best rooms in {hall} are being made ready.

options.label: Send gifts, but stay at Kingsmere
options.result: The crown sends silver and its regrets. The wedding goes ahead without the King.

beats.speaker: host
beats.text: A kitchen girl from {hall} reaches Kingsmere half-dead from riding: when the musicians play the old wedding song, {host}'s men will bar the doors.

court.text: A servant girl kneels, shaking: "Your Grace, my lord {host} means to murder them all at the feast. When the music turns, the doors close."

options.label: Warn {guest} in secret
options.result: A royal rider reaches {guest} on the road to {hall}. {guest.house} turns back.

options.label: Ride to {hall} with the royal guard and sit at the high table (200 gold)
options.result: The King arrives at {hall} with a hundred guards. {host} smiles, and tells the musicians to play something else.

options.label: Say nothing: let them settle their own feud
options.result: The King says nothing. The girl is sent back to {hall}.

beats.speaker: host
beats.text: The musicians play the old wedding song. The doors of {hall} close, and {guest.house}'s lords die at the table. The realm will call it the Red Feast for a hundred years.

die.how: murdered at the Red Feast in {hall}

court.text: {host} kneels with blood still under {host.his} nails: "It is done, Your Grace. {guest.house} was a danger to your peace. I ask only the crown's pardon, and {guesthall}."

options.label: Pardon {host}
options.hint: {host.houseName} +15 · every house learns what the crown permits
options.result: The King pardons {host}. No great lord will ever again accept a wedding invitation without a hundred swords.

options.label: Name {host} a murderer and an outlaw
options.hint: {host.houseName} −40 · {host} has an army and nothing to lose
options.result: Heralds cry {host}'s crime in every town. In {hall}, {host} sharpens the swords that did it.

beats.speaker: host
beats.text: Outlawed, {host} has nothing left to lose, and marches on Kingsmere with the swords that did the Red Feast.

beats.speaker: guest
beats.text: There is no Red Feast. {guest.house} lives, owes the crown its life, and never sits at {host}'s table again.

beats.speaker: host
beats.text: {host} keeps {guesthall} and the King's pardon. The realm keeps the memory, and the crown keeps a lord who knows its price.
The murderer of the Red Feast is broken before Kingsmere. The dead of {guest.house} are answered.
